exception_description: No PO referenced on invoice.
root_cause_hypothesis: The internal business unit likely bypassed the standard procurement process, resulting in the vendor submitting an invoice without a required PO number. This could be due to an urgent purchase or lack of awareness of the 'No PO, No Pay' policy.
recommended_action: Contact the assigned approver, Jane Smith, to validate the charge and determine the business owner. A retroactive PO or formal management exception is required due to the high invoice value.
communication_draft:
Hi team,

Hope you're having a good week. This is an urgent follow-up from Accounts Payable regarding an invoice from Global Tech.

Invoice ID: SAP-9002
Vendor: Global Tech
Amount: $95,000.00

This payment is currently on hold as there was no Purchase Order referenced. To ensure the vendor is paid on time, could you please raise a PO for this invoice and send us the number?

As per our internal SLA, we need the PO to be raised within the next 3 business days to release the payment.

Please let me know if you have any questions. Thanks for your urgent attention to this matter.

exception_description: Server hardware invoice $44
approver_assigned: 200. Variance of 8.0% — exceeds 5% threshold. Finance Controller review needed.
root_cause_hypothesis: The 8% variance on a large hardware order suggests either a price increase from the vendor post-PO approval or the inclusion of unbudgeted costs like expedited shipping or taxes. This was not reflected in an updated PO before invoicing.
recommended_action: Contact the business requester and procurement team to investigate the discrepancy, validate the charges with the vendor, and obtain a revised PO or formal approval for the variance.
communication_draft:
This note is to request your review and approval for a high-priority invoice exception.

Invoice INV-2026-014 from Dell Technologies for $44,500.00 has a significant price variance of 8% against PO-6612. This server hardware invoice has now been outstanding for 50 days.

The root cause appears to be a vendor price increase or unbudgeted costs added after the PO was approved. Due to the high value and variance percentage, this exception exceeds standard AP approval thresholds and requires Controller sign-off. Standard resolution attempts with the business requester and procurement team have been unsuccessful in obtaining a revised PO.

To avoid further payment delays and potential vendor relationship issues, we request your decision within two business days. Please advise if we should continue to pursue a revised PO from procurement or if you will provide formal approval for the existing variance.

exception_description: Invoice amount exceeds PO value by 8.3%. PO approved for $39
root_cause_hypothesis: The vendor's invoice amount is 8.3% higher than the approved PO amount. This could be due to a price increase not reflected in the PO, additional unapproved services, or a vendor billing error.
recommended_action: Route invoice to the PO approver to validate the price difference and either approve the variance or dispute the charge with the vendor.
communication_draft:
This is a formal escalation for a high-priority invoice exception requiring your immediate attention.

Invoice INV-2026-001 from SAP SE for $42,500.00 has a price variance of $3,250.00 (8.3%) above its approved purchase order, PO-9821. This invoice is critically aged at 250 days outstanding, posing a risk to vendor relations and financial reporting.

The root cause appears to be a price increase not reflected in the PO, additional unapproved services, or a vendor billing error. Standard approval workflows are insufficient due to the age and value of the variance, necessitating your review.

Our recommended action is to route the invoice to the PO approver to validate the price difference and determine whether to approve the variance or dispute the charge.

We request your decision on this recommendation within two business days to resolve this long-outstanding issue.

exception_description: Data warehouse usage charges $37
approver_assigned: 000. Variance of 6.3% — exceeds 5% threshold for escalation.
root_cause_hypothesis: The invoice is for usage-based cloud services where actual consumption exceeded the initial estimate on the purchase order. This is common for variable spend categories like data warehousing.
recommended_action: Route to the PO approver/business owner to confirm usage and approve the budget increase. A PO change order is required.
communication_draft:
This note is to request your urgent attention for a high-priority, aged invoice exception.

Invoice INV-2026-020 from Snowflake Inc. for $37,200.00 has now been outstanding for 200 days. Payment is blocked due to a significant price variance against the corresponding Purchase Order, PO-1157.

The root cause is that actual consumption for usage-based cloud services exceeded the initial estimate on the PO. This scenario is common for variable spend categories like data warehousing and requires budget owner confirmation.

Given the value and significant age of this payable, this exception requires senior financial approval to proceed.

We recommend routing the invoice to the business owner to confirm usage and approve the required budget increase. A PO change order would then be processed.

To resolve this matter and mitigate vendor relationship risk, we request your decision on this action within two business days.

exception_description: AWS compute and storage invoice exceeds PO by 1.4%. Within auto-approve threshold — minimal risk.
root_cause_hypothesis: The variance is likely due to fluctuations in cloud service consumption that exceeded the initial PO estimate. This is common for utility-based services like AWS where usage can be variable.
recommended_action: Route to assigned approver, David Kim, for review and approval of the 1.4% variance, noting it falls within expected thresholds for this vendor type.
communication_draft:
This is a formal escalation for a high-priority price variance exception on Invoice INV-2026-010 from Amazon Web Services. The invoice for $33,800.00 has been outstanding for 3 days.

The invoice amount exceeds the associated PO-1166 by 1.4%. The root cause is a slight overage in cloud service consumption, which is a common and expected fluctuation for this type of utility-based service.

Although this variance is minimal and within standard tolerance, the system has flagged it, requiring your sign-off to proceed. We are escalating for your awareness and to clear the exception queue for this high-value supplier.

Our recommendation is to approve the variance, which will allow the invoice to be routed to the assigned approver, David Kim, for final business review. This action presents minimal risk and will prevent payment delays.

Please provide your decision within two business days to ensure timely payment to this critical vendor.

exception_description: Annual HR platform renewal invoice received without a purchase order. Contract renewal not yet raised in procurement system.
root_cause_hypothesis: This is a recurring contractual expense for an annual software renewal. The business owner failed to initiate the procurement process to raise a PO before the vendor's invoice was received.
recommended_action: Contact approver David Kim to urgently raise a purchase order for the Workday annual renewal to unblock payment.
communication_draft:
Hi David,

A quick and urgent heads-up from the AP team.

We are holding payment for an overdue invoice from **Workday Inc (INV-2026-006)** for $28,000.00. This is for your annual HR platform renewal, but it was received without a corresponding Purchase Order.

The invoice is now 31 days outstanding. To avoid any further delays or issues with the vendor, could you please raise a PO for this in the procurement system?

As per our policy, the PO must be raised within the next **3 business days**. We will process the payment immediately once the approved PO is received.

Thanks for your prompt attention to this matter.

exception_description: Google Cloud Platform invoice for Q2 infrastructure with no matching PO. IT raised request verbally but no formal PO created.

recommended_action: Contact the IT department and approver Maria Lopez to create and approve a retroactive purchase order for this invoice.

exception_description: Professional services invoice $19
approver_assigned: 800. Variance of 15.5% — high severity escalation required.
root_cause_hypothesis: The vendor billed for additional services or hours not included in the original PO, representing scope creep that was not formally approved via a PO update. This is common for professional services contracts.
recommended_action: Contact the PO owner/business approver to validate the additional charges and provide approval for the 15.5% variance.
communication_draft:
This note is to request your urgent intervention for a high-priority exception on invoice INV-2026-007 from ServiceNow for $19,400.00. The invoice has been outstanding for 400 days.

The issue is a significant price variance of 15.5% over the approved amount on PO-4401. Our investigation indicates the root cause is scope creep; the vendor billed for professional services not included in the original purchase order. This overage was not formally approved via a PO update.

Due to the size of the variance and the extended aging of this invoice, standard resolution paths have been exhausted. This escalation requires Controller-level sign-off to either approve the variance for payment or provide direction on next steps. The business owner must validate the additional charges before payment can be considered.

Your decision on how to proceed is requested within two business days to mitigate further vendor relationship risk and resolve this long-outstanding item.

exception_description: No purchase order number found on invoice. Vendor submitted directly without prior approval.

recommended_action: Route invoice to assigned approver James Patel to either create a retroactive PO or provide a valid cost center and documented approval for payment.

exception_description: Payment processing vendor not in approved vendor master. Previously used under a parent entity — subsidiary not registered.
root_cause_hypothesis: The vendor is a subsidiary of an existing approved vendor but was not formally added to the vendor master list. This indicates a gap in the vendor onboarding process when dealing with corporate subsidiaries.
recommended_action: Contact procurement to initiate the vendor onboarding process for 'Stripe Inc.' and place the invoice on hold pending vendor master file setup.
communication_draft:
Hi Procurement Team,

We are requesting your assistance with invoice INV-2026-019 from Stripe Inc for $12,400.00, which is now 21 days outstanding.

The invoice was approved by Maria Lopez, but we cannot process it because Stripe Inc is not registered in our approved vendor master. We understand this may be a subsidiary of a registered parent entity, but this specific entity is not set up for payment.

As a result, payment for this invoice is currently blocked.

To resolve this, could you please either initiate the formal vendor onboarding process for Stripe Inc or confirm the correct, approved entity that should be used for this service?

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

exception_description: Possible duplicate of INV-2026-009 processed last month. Same vendor

recommended_action: Verify payment status of the original invoice INV-2026-009. If already paid, reject this invoice and notify the vendor to prevent future occurrences.
communication_draft:

exception_description: Vendor listed under trading name different from registered entity in vendor master. Requires procurement verification.

recommended_action: Engage the Procurement team to verify the vendor's trading name and update the vendor master file with the correct alias.

During processing, we discovered the vendor's trading name on the invoice does not match a registered legal entity in our vendor master. As per AP policy, we cannot issue payment to an unverified vendor entity.

Could you please investigate this matter? We require you to either confirm the correct, existing vendor entity to process this payment against, or initiate the onboarding process if this is a new legal entity.

This invoice is now 6 days outstanding, and payment will remain blocked until we receive your verification.

Thank you for your prompt assistance in resolving this.

exception_description: SMS API usage invoice $1

exception_description: Invoice shows 45 licences at $197.78 each but PO authorised only 38 licences. Overbilling by 7 units.

recommended_action: Contact approver Maria Lopez to confirm if the 7 additional licenses are valid and, if so, request a PO amendment to match the invoiced quantity.
communication_draft:
Dear Salesforce Accounts Receivable Team,

We are writing in reference to invoice INV-2026-003, which is associated with our purchase order PO-7743.

Upon review, we have identified a quantity discrepancy. The invoice bills for 45 licenses, whereas our purchase order only authorized the purchase of 38 licenses. This has resulted in an overbilling of 7 units.

Payment for this invoice is currently on hold pending correction. To resolve this, please provide either a credit note for the 7 excess units or a revised invoice that accurately reflects the 38 units authorized on our PO.

We kindly request a response or the updated document within 5 business days to ensure timely processing.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Sincerely,

Accounts Payable Team
